ground_truth_witness: Alphabet 2^Xi with Xi = {P1E, P2E, P1C, P2C}. Violating word sigma = {P1E,P2E} . {}^omega with i = 0: sigma,0 |= P1E & P2E and sigma,0 |/= F(P1C|P2C), so sigma,0 |/= (P1E&P2E) -> F(P1C|P2C); hence sigma_hat = sigma[..0] = {P1E,P2E} is exactly the finite prefix the proof declares a bad prefix. Repairing extension: sigma' = {P1E,P2E} . ({P1C})^omega, which has sigma_hat as a prefix and satisfies sigma',0 |= P1E & P2E and sigma',0 |= F(P1C|P2C), therefore sigma',0 |= (P1E&P2E) -> F(P1C|P2C). Claim says: sigma',i |/= (P1E&P2E) -> F(P1C|P2C) for ALL extensions sigma' of sigma_hat; here the implication is SATISFIED at i = 0, so the claim fails on this witness. The same failure occurs for every admissible (sigma_hat, i) pair found: 357/357 admissible pairs (273/273 with i = |sigma_hat|-1) admit a repairing extension inside the searched lasso family; none lacked one.
ground_truth_flaw: In the safety-property argument, the author claims that any extension σ' of the finite prefix σ̂ = σ[..i] still violates the implication at position i, i.e., σ',i ⊭ (P1E ∧ P2E) → F(P1C ∨ P2C), so σ̂ is a bad prefix. This is false: satisfaction of F(P1C ∨ P2C) at position i depends on the infinite suffix beyond the prefix, so an extension can repair the violation.
